newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said her government would take steps to reform concerned laws to help flourish the nation's cultural heritage and restore "spirit and values" of liberation war.

Lead content in Dhaka's air during low-rain period is one of the highest in the world, according to a 17-month analysis carried out by a group of scientists of the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission. The scientists detected 463 nanogram (billionth of a gram) per cubic metre of air during November to January. Second in the list is Mexico with a concentration of 383, they said.

Bangladesh has moved a proposal for a sub-regional economic bloc comprising Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and India's West Bengal and northeastern states. Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad, during his recent visit to West Bengal and Myanmar, proposed the idea. Azad said he got positive response.
The government would create permanent fish sanctuaries across the country to preserve rare species of fish, State Minister for Land Rashed Mosharraf said.

Bangladesh Islami Bank Ltd (BIBL) will launch a Tk 2 billion ($50 million) savings bond scheme by November this yar to encourage savings through sharing a portion of the profit. BIBL will be the first banking institution to float savings bonds in Bangladesh.
